title: Onboarded Model Handshake Spec and Deprecation Policy
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Define a machine-readable 'handshake' manifest and an explicit deprecation policy for pinned model versions to guarantee stable prompt formats, output shapes, parameter aliases, and performance envelopes for customers who pin models.
background: Customers pin model versions to avoid surprise regressions. We lack a canonical artifact and process that (a) declares input/output schemas and parameter aliases, (b) enumerates allowed performance optimizations, and (c) provides an auditable deprecation/migration path. This work synthesizes a spec, enforcement checks, release gating, and customer communications for pinned releases.
proposal: Introduce a 'handshake manifest' (schema v1) as part of model onboarding. Manifest is attached to pinned model metadata and is immutable for a pinned release.
Manifest fields: prompt_schema, output_schema, parameter_alias_map, default_hyperparams, perf_profile (latency/cost envelope), compatibility_level, signed_manifest_hash, and churn_history_url.
Define compatibility_level semantics: "stable-io" (no input/output changes), "stable-behavior" (small prob. deltas allowed), and "breaking" (requires deprecation flow).
Enforce manifest at three touchpoints: onboarding acceptance tests, runtime input/output validator (best-effort), and Console UI display for customers who pin versions.
Allowed runtime optimizations (quantization, kernel selection) must be declared in perf_profile and validated against perf regression thresholds before manifest can be promoted to 'published'.

Deprecation policy: any change marked 'breaking' must follow a minimum 90-day deprecation window, include migration examples, automated golden-set diffs, and an opt-in early access flag for customers to test the new variant.
Provide a manifest-signing process (CI artifact signed by release team key) and persist signatures in release metadata so clients and internal tooling can verify authenticity.
Add automatic fallback routing: if a runtime detects unexpected output-shape mismatch for a pinned model, route to last-known-compatible variant and surface an incident to the owner.
Deliver a migration toolkit (prompt adapters + parameter alias translations) and a template release note generator for product and support teams.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc for handshake manifest v1 reviewed and approved by Eng + PM + Security.
Onboarding CI runs a manifest-based regression suite that covers golden-set output diffs, token-cost delta, and latency percentiles; failure blocks promotion.
Console shows manifest fields and compatibility_level for pinned model pages; signed_manifest_hash is visible in metadata.
Runtime can detect output-shape violations and execute configured fallback routing in canary environments.
Deprecation flow exists in Playbook form (timeline, customer comms, migration artifacts) and a sample deprecation has been exercised in staging.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Implement manifest schema and onboarding CI checks; run with newly onboarded internal models only.
Phase 2 (canary): Enable manifest enforcement for a small percentage of hosted customers; monitor regressions and fallback activations.
Phase 3 (GA): Require signed manifest for all new pinned releases; surface manifest metadata in Console and API responses for pinned variants.
Phase 4 (deprecation trials): Execute a controlled breaking change deprecation flow with one internal partner and gather feedback before wider rollout.
tests_and_evals: Golden-set regression harness: per-model prompt set with deterministic scoring and output-shape checks.
Perf regression tests: token-cost and P95 latency checks run under representative load profiles; budget delta thresholds defined per model family.
Alias resolution tests: verify parameter_alias_map translates legacy parameter names to canonical names across SDKs.
End-to-end canary test that intentionally introduces a shape change to validate runtime fallback and incident generation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Models with nondeterministic outputs may show spurious diffs. Mitigation: use probabilistic thresholds and semantic similarity metrics (ROUGE/Embed-sim) with manual review triggers.

Risk: Customers rely on implicit parameter behavior that isn't captured in manifest. Mitigation: require onboarding questionnaire and surface 'implicit-behavior' flags in manifest; build adapter helpers.
Risk: Increased onboarding friction. Mitigation: provide templates, auto-generated manifest drafts from onboarding pipeline, and one-click accept in Console for internal QA runs.
Risk: Manifest signing adds operational burden. Mitigation: integrate with existing release CI and KMS for automated key rotation and audit logs.
